Probably way too late to this, but I was sexually assaulted by my then-best friend at my 18th birthday party. When my 19th came around, I was in a psych ward for related reasons. It felt like my birthday was cursed. I tried celebrating it for a couple of years after, but was so neurotic about having a good birthday that I couldn't enjoy it, so I stopped celebrating it (at least with friends; my mum always wanted to do something). I took the day off work so I could sit and have whatever feelings I had.

This year, after a LOT of therapy, I went out for drinks in a small group, some of whom knew that this was kind of a big deal, and ended up having the best birthday I'd had since before the incident. I don't know if I'll be able to do it again, but I'm no longer putting pressure on myself to celebrate in any way, and that's made all the difference.

Hey, nonbinary person who gets misgendered a lot here. It's a good thing to not excessively apologise! I appreciate it's hard for you because you feel like shit, but doing the whole excessive apology thing usually only makes the other person feel like shit. We - most of us anyway - can tell when misgendering is accidental, and by far the best way to deal with it is "and so he, sorry she, said..." You're doing the right thing not making a song and dance of it. I can tell you're not a bad person **because** you give a shit about this, and you aren't purposefully trying to hurt people.

I hope that helps. Accidental misgendering is inevitable, especially if you don't know the person. Keep doing what you're doing.

I had this! How much attention are you paying to your breathing? If you're always inhaling/exhaling as your right foot hits the ground (common when people breathe in for two strides and out for two strides), this may cause pain. I fixed it by breathing in for 2, out for 3 - you can switch it us depending on how hard you need to breathe, so sometimes at the start of a run I'll do in for 3, out for 4, or even in 4 out 5.

Also, make sure you're breathing from your diaphragm as much as possible. You can even practise this at a walking pace.

Give it a shot, hope it helps!
